messages:
Maya Chen: Quick follow-up on the on-prem delta package RFC. I'm leaning toward a signed manifest + chunked deltas with an explicit apply-plan. Thoughts on atomicity and rollout safety?
Luis Ortega: Atomic apply is a hard requirement for airgapped customers. If a subset fails we must auto-revert; no chance to fetch fixes.
Priya Nair: Two-phase approach seems pragmatic: stage artifacts under /opt/redwood/staged/<ver> then swap a symlink to activate after verification. That gives an instant rollback path.
Jin Park: Symlink swap works for disk layout but watch long-running processes. We need a pre-swap health-check and graceful drain hook, otherwise in-memory binaries could mismatch.
Maya Chen: Exactly — propose: 1) stage, 2) run pre-swap health & smoke, 3) swap symlink atomically, 4) post-swap functional checks, 5) finalize or revert.
Luis Ortega: Another trade: full-image bundles vs chunked deltas. Deltas smaller for customers but migrations/DB schema changes make deltas riskier.
Priya Nair: Mitigate with explicit migration scripts bundled separately and a migration manifest with sha256 and idempotency hints. Example manifest snippet:
```yaml
- name: db-migration-34.sql
  sha256: 3a7d...
  size: 12KB
  prereq: ">=2.1.0 <3.0.0"
  post-check: "psql -c \"SELECT 1 FROM migrations WHERE id=34\""
```
ops-qa-bot: ops-qa-bot: note: must include an offline verification tool in the bundle. Suggest command: `redwood-verify bundle.tar.gz --trusted-keys /mnt/keys`.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: notice: test bundle 1843125600 applied to staging-cluster-3 (automated smoke run started).
Maya Chen: For rollback policy: auto-revert on failed post-check seems necessary for unattended installs. For controlled enterprise installs, provide `--manual-approve`.
Jin Park: Agreed. Auto revert should attempt 2 retries then revert and write a failure report bundle for ops. Include a human-readable error code in /var/log/redwood/upgrade.log.
Priya Nair: We should also embed lightweight quality checks — small eval vectors for model-serving and routing tests. If quality regresses beyond threshold, abort apply.
Luis Ortega: Edge-case: power loss mid-apply. We need resumable, idempotent chunking. Each chunk must have a sequence number and txn log so apply can resume/rollback cleanly.
Maya Chen: Proposal: store apply state at /var/lib/redwood/upgrade-state.json with fields: sequence, applied_chunks, staged_path. Keep it simple JSON so ops can inspect.
Priya Nair: Also include a signature chain: bundle.tar.gz.sig referencing manifest.sig which references root key. We'll use sigstore-style detached signatures to make offline validation deterministic.
ops-qa-bot: Operational note: telemetry disabled in airgapped mode. Add `redwood-diagnostics --collect` to generate an attachable diagnostics bundle for support.
Maya Chen: Action items: I'll update the RFC with stager + symlink activation, manifest schema, verify tool, resumable chunking, and auto-revert behavior. @Luis Ortega to draft manifest schema, @Priya Nair to prototype the verify tool.
Luis Ortega: On it. I'll post a WIP manifest schema in #eng-runtime by EOD Tue.
Priya Nair: I'll prototype a minimal `redwood-verify` binary that checks sha256 + signature chain and emits a json report.
Maya Chen: Thanks — let's re-sync Thursday 11:00. If anyone sees missing failure modes (power loss, partial disk, failed migration idempotency) call them out here. :thumbsup:
